data.name: Awe of Despair
data.detailed_description:
Awe of Despair é um jogo de horror de sobrevivência que o coloca no lugar de um homem que decide ignorar o estigma do número 13. O objetivo deste jogo é proporcionar ao jogador uma experiência de horror profundamente imersiva. Awe of Despair é um atirador de terror de sobrevivência em primeira pessoa. Você acorda em um apartamento e rapidamente percebe que coisas estranhas acontecem. Você vai se deparar com criaturas perturbadoras, descobrir armas e resolver enigmas enquanto você luta para sair deste mundo paralelo.


Este jogo não é adequado para crianças ou aqueles que são facilmente perturbados.


Awe of Despair não é traduzido para outros idiomas além do inglês. Várias traduções estão em breve. O jogo tem texto e texto em inglês mínimo, portanto, o jogo deve ser jogável para a maioria das pessoas que falam outros idiomas.

reviews.review:
Awe of Despair is currently the sole release from new indie developer/publisher, Reliant. The game can be classified as a light survival horror snack, with sprinkles of psychological horror elements throughout. Players wake up in a small apartment, and with no story or instructions to go on they must find their way through three levels; the apartment complex, the morgue, and the basement.

The scares and monster spawns in Awe of Despair seem to be randomly generated, as each time the player dies and wakes up at the nearest spawn point the enemies seem to change. It's very difficult to discern exactly what needs to be done in order to trigger any sort of progression, and it easily creates confusing gameplay that ultimately leads to a lot of unnecessary frustration. In the elevator, located on the apartment level, I became stuck despite having input the correct code. It was only after restarting the game that I was finally able to move forward to the next level; the morgue. The second level also held problems for me, with a monster that killed me despite having loaded about 20 bullets into him.

The game also makes you choose between having a weapon out, or your flashlight out. This wouldn't be as big of an issue if it weren't for the fact that all of the enemies are nearly pitch black, and the game itself is extremely dark even with the brightness pumped all the way up to max. There's also a lot of weird graphical flaws, and much of the assets and environments have a weird grey effect on them that's akin to viewing a low-viewing-angle TV from the side. There are also elements in the trailer on the store page that I could not find in the game; namely the shotgun, and the hanging body.

In the end, Awe of Despair has some great ideas. It's one of the few indie horror games that've actually made me utter a few screams. It's great at catching players off guard, and the random spawns and different scare tactics are refreshing. However, ultimately the game has zero focus; the lack of handholding is the biggest downfall here, and it's not very fun to just run around the same areas trying to trigger the next event. It's also a hard game even on the easiest difficulty, especially during the morgue where it's easy to get overrun by foes. With a bit more shine and polish, Awe of Despair could be something great. Until then, however, it's hard to recommend it due to just how confusing and convoluted it can be.

[h1]Rating: [b]2.0/5.0[/b] - It's not awful, but it's not great.[/h1]
